topics.topic: Catch-up, deduplication, and overlap rules for scheduled backups
questions: Are missed runs caught up on startup, and what happens when a scheduled run overlaps an earlier run?
When is a missed daily run performed, and how is a second run on the same UTC day prevented?
What happens when Registry is stopped at 03:00 UTC or remains stopped for several scheduled days?

quotes: Registry backs up its store once a day at 03:00 UTC into the backup location, as a consistent copy taken while it runs: a backup never holds part of a transaction.
A backup or a deletion that fails leaves no partial file, writes a diagnostic that names the failure and no value (A17), and is tried again at the next run; Registry keeps serving.
judgement.divergence: One implementation catches up a missed run on startup and serialises or skips overlaps, while another skips missed runs and may start overlapping or repeated same-day runs; the owner notices different backup availability, retention deletion times and restore points.
judgement.why: The scheduling rule leaves downtime, restart, deduplication and overlap behaviour open.

topics.topic: Imported customer identity, required records, and customer_ref allocation
questions: Does a distinct v1 `customer_ref` implicitly count as a customer the file holds, or must the export contain a separate Customer record?
Does the VPS import ever preserve an incoming customer_ref or require Customer records in the file, or does every distinct v1 value always generate a new Customer as M04 says?
Is each new customer_ref minted and displayed in the mapping, reserved until confirmation, or minted only inside the import transaction?

quotes: The owner also says whether the v1 value is the Customer's tax id; one that is not is shown in the import's mapping and kept nowhere.
The import makes one new Customer for each distinct v1 value and links every imported project that named it to that Customer.

A brought-in record is malformed when: a required value is missing (A02); it names a project, customer or room the file does not hold; an id occurs twice among the file's records of one kind; a status is outside its vocabulary, or a pointer is `withdrawn` (v1 never withdrew one, M05); a pointer's type is not declared or its owner service is not the type's (A22); the versions of a project's pointers of one type are not 1..n, or more than one of them is `published`, or a `superseded` one is not lower than a later version; an instant cannot be read; an `active` project has an archived instant or an `archived` one has none; a `superseded` pointer has no superseded instant or a `published` one has one; a record was changed, archived or superseded before it was created, added or published.

Any conflict — a project, room or pointer id production holds, a Registry-minted `customer_ref` production holds — or any malformed record refuses the whole import, and nothing changes (R0-50, R0-79).

Registry reads it as data (A19) and answers the mapping without changing anything: each project the file holds, with its id, status, rooms and pointers; for each project the owner picks, the display name and alias it will arrive under (R0-85); each Customer the import will make, with the v1 value it comes from and the projects it will link (R0-80); every id that conflicts with one production holds.
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats each distinct legacy value as sufficient to create a Customer and mints its new identity only in the committing transaction; another requires an incoming Customer record or preserved reference and may allocate and expose the new identity during preview, so the owner sees different mappings and the same file is accepted by one implementation but refused by the other.
judgement.why: The rules do not reconcile legacy values with the requirement that referenced customers be present, nor state when the new identity is allocated.
judgement.failure: the quoted passage of a consequential gap is not found verbatim in the texts

topics.topic: Multiplicity, namespace, and replacement of pending confirmation values
questions: What is the namespace and replacement rule for pending confirmation values?
May one owner session hold several live confirmation values, and if so, which existing value is replaced when another confirmation step is shown?
When is a pending confirmation value replaced, and may one owner session hold several live values for different actions or targets at once?

quotes: changed by the owner's requests: the instant of its last request, its pending confirmation values and the import file uploaded in it, each kept until used, replaced or the session ends (State 2 A13, A16; owner, 2026-10-31).

An action that asks for confirmation (Identity formats) is submitted with a confirmation value Registry made when it showed the step: one-time, kept in the owner session, bound to the action, its target, the revision or access version the step showed, and its inputs — for the import, the file's digest and the picks.
judgement.divergence: One implementation permits several confirmation values keyed by action and target, while another keeps only one and replaces it whenever any new confirmation step is shown; the owner notices whether an older open confirmation page still works.
judgement.why: The texts acknowledge replacement and plural pending values without defining their multiplicity or replacement key.

topics.topic: Owner-session idle-clock initialization and meaning of the last-request instant
questions: What value initializes the idle clock, and are “last request” and `last_action` the same session fact?
From what instant does the 30-minute idle limit run before the session's first post-sign-in request?
At sign-in, what value initializes the session's last-request instant before the owner makes another request?

quotes: changed by the owner's requests: the instant of its last request, its pending confirmation values and the import file uploaded in it, each kept until used, replaced or the session ends (State 2 A13, A16; owner, 2026-10-31).
The session ends at the first of: 8 hours after sign-in; 30 minutes without an owner request; the owner's sign-out; the instance's restart (M11 is never durable).
An owner request is any request to the owner interface that carries the valid session, whatever its answer; it restarts the 30 minutes.

owner_session s valid at t <=> t < s.began + 8h and
                                t < s.last_action + 30min and
                                not signed_out(s) and no restart since s.began
judgement.divergence: One implementation initializes the last-request instant to the sign-in instant, while another leaves it unset or starts the idle clock only on the first authenticated post-sign-in request; the owner notices different expiry before that first request.
judgement.why: The idle rule uses an unstated initial value and two names without declaring that they denote the same fact.

topics.topic: Authenticated backup encryption scheme and metadata format
questions: What exact authenticated backup format and cryptographic algorithm must Registry use, and how does it identify the key and format needed to decrypt an older backup?
What exact authenticated-encryption scheme and metadata format must implementations use?

quotes: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
judgement.why: The algorithm, nonce, authenticated envelope, key identifier and cryptographic-version representation are encoding and file-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Evidence criteria required for each security-review category
questions: What criteria must be checked for each category so the claim that the review is complete can be verified from the design texts alone?
What exact questions or evidence criteria must be satisfied for each category to justify the stated APPLICABLE or NOT_APPLICABLE outcome?

quotes: The categories are the nine of the Workbench's security review (`skills/spec-authoring/SECURITY_REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md`), the catalogue every case is reviewed against; this review is complete for that catalogue and claims nothing beyond it.
Each category has exactly one outcome below, resting on the decisions it names.
Each APPLICABLE category's decisions have their own required tests, and those tests pass.
judgement.divergence: One reviewer treats naming decisions and passing their listed tests as sufficient evidence, while another applies additional category-specific questions from the referenced catalogue; the owner notices different review outcomes and release readiness.
judgement.why: The claimed complete State 2 review depends on category criteria that the accepted texts neither state nor make independently verifiable.

topics.topic: Import preview sequence and regeneration when picks or replacements change
questions: What exact request sequence produces the final mapping that the confirmation value binds?
When and how are picks and replacement values supplied relative to upload, mapping display and confirmation, and does changing any of them require Registry to generate a new mapping?

quotes: The owner uploads the export file (R0-72) in the owner interface.

Registry reads it as data (A19) and answers the mapping without changing anything: each project the file holds, with its id, status, rooms and pointers; for each project the owner picks, the display name and alias it will arrive under (R0-85); each Customer the import will make, with the v1 value it comes from and the projects it will link (R0-80); every id that conflicts with one production holds.

The owner confirms that mapping in the confirmation step (A13 rule 6); the confirmation applies the file of that digest, the picks, names, aliases and Customer values the mapping showed, nothing else; a file no longer kept is refused and must be uploaded again.
judgement.why: The exact owner-interface request sequence and regeneration flow belong to the later state that defines flows and public API interactions.

topics.topic: Owner-session cookie attributes and same-site transport policy
questions: Which exact cookie attributes and cross-site sending policy enforce “only to Registry’s own origin”?
What exact cookie attributes and same-site policy enforce these statements, and may the cookie be sent over plain HTTP when Registry is reached locally?

quotes: The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only to Registry's own origin.
judgement.why: Exact cookie attributes, host/path scope and SameSite transport policy are HTTP contract and encoding details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Permitted state when deletion of an expired or invalid backup fails
questions: What guarantee holds when deleting an expired backup fails?
What state and classification does an invalid backup have if Registry cannot delete its file?
What state is permitted after deletion of an expired or failed-verification backup fails?

quotes: A backup that fails the check is deleted and counts as failed.
A backup or a deletion that fails leaves no partial file, writes a diagnostic that names the failure and no value (A17), and is tried again at the next run; Registry keeps serving.

after a run: no backup older than 30 days exists
every kept backup is encrypted, consistent, checked, and records
  (instant, release, last sequence); no backup holds an agent session
judgement.why: The normative rule permits a failed deletion to leave an expired or invalid file until the next run, while the formal invariant permits no old or unchecked kept backup after a run.

topics.topic: Representation used to measure configured secret byte lengths
questions: How is the 32-byte minimum measured for owner credentials, service tokens and the backup key?
Which representation is measured when configuration supplies text: encoded bytes, decoded binary bytes, or characters, and which encoding or decoding is required?

quotes: A secret — each token, the owner credential and the backup key — is at least 32 bytes long; a shorter one fails the start.
judgement.why: The textual or binary representation, encoding and decoding used to measure byte length are field-type and encoding contracts owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Results of concurrent create calls with equal or different request ids
questions: Does A07's two-publication rule apply only when the concurrent calls carry different request ids?
What are the exact results when two concurrent creates of the same model first present the same request id, with equal or different facts?

quotes: A create whose request id an existing record of the same model carries is a repeat when the facts it supplies equal that record's current facts of the same kind: Registry answers the record as it stands now and changes nothing.

A create whose request id an existing record carries, with facts that differ from that record's current ones — a different value, or the record corrected since — is refused, and nothing changes; the caller reads the record.

Two concurrent publishes of a type are both accepted with consecutive versions; a withdrawal that runs after a publish superseded its pointer is refused as withdrawing a superseded pointer; a publish that runs after a withdrawal makes the next version `published`; a second withdrawal of one pointer is refused.
judgement.divergence: One implementation atomically reserves each request id so equal concurrent calls yield one record and differing calls yield one success plus one refusal, while another races before either record exists and may reject both, fail internally or attempt two records; the callers notice different answers and record counts.
judgement.why: The repeat rule presumes an existing record but does not specify serialization or winner behaviour for simultaneous first use of one request id.

topics.topic: Validation and conflict-checking scope for unpicked import records
questions: Must Registry inspect and report conflicts and malformed data in unpicked projects when producing the mapping?
Does an unpicked record participate in duplicate-id, reference and production-conflict checks when it collides with a picked record?

quotes: Registry reads it as data (A19) and answers the mapping without changing anything: each project the file holds, with its id, status, rooms and pointers; for each project the owner picks, the display name and alias it will arrive under (R0-85); each Customer the import will make, with the v1 value it comes from and the projects it will link (R0-80); every id that conflicts with one production holds.

Registry checks what the picks bring in — the picked projects with their rooms and pointers and the customers they name — and nothing else of the file; records only of projects the owner did not pick are neither checked nor imported.
A conflicting id belonging only to a project the owner did not pick does not refuse the import.
judgement.why: The mapping rule requires every production conflict to be reported, while the scope rule says records belonging only to unpicked projects are not checked.

topics.topic: Validity of an old import confirmation after file replacement
questions: When a confirmation for the old digest is submitted after a replacement upload, is it refused or can the old file still be applied?
Must confirmation of the old mapping be refused because its file was dropped, or must Registry retain and apply the old file rather than the newly uploaded one?

quotes: The uploaded file is kept in the owner session that uploaded it, never in the store, until the import is confirmed, another file is uploaded in that session, or the session ends (M11); then it is dropped.
Confirming a mapping after another file was uploaded applies only the file whose digest the confirmation named.
judgement.why: One passage drops the old file when another is uploaded, while the required test says a later confirmation applies the file named by the old mapping's digest.

topics.topic: Whether refused import confirmation consumes the uploaded file
questions: Does a confirmation submission that passes session and CSRF checks but is later refused also drop the uploaded import file?
Does a refused confirmation submission count as using the uploaded import file, or does it consume only the confirmation value while retaining the file for a newly shown confirmation step?

quotes: changed by the owner's requests: the instant of its last request, its pending confirmation values and the import file uploaded in it, each kept until used, replaced or the session ends (State 2 A13, A16; owner, 2026-10-31).

The uploaded file is kept in the owner session that uploaded it, never in the store, until the import is confirmed, another file is uploaded in that session, or the session ends (M11); then it is dropped.

A submission becomes the first one when it passes the owner session and CSRF checks (A04 rule 6, stage 1): one refused before them leaves the value unused; from there on, whatever the answer — a value bound to another action included — the value is used up.
judgement.divergence: One implementation retains the uploaded file after a refused confirmation and allows the owner to obtain a new confirmation step, while another treats the submission as use of both the value and file and requires re-upload; the owner notices the extra upload and whether the retained mapping can be retried.
judgement.why: The texts define consumption of the confirmation value but use incompatible stopping terms for the uploaded file without saying whether a refused confirmation uses it.
